div.head: I Atr 1.3
div.ab: Gif se að þonne forðcume, ceose se man þonne, þe þær betyhtlet sy, swa hweðer he wylle swa anfeald ordal swa pundes wurþne að innan þam þrim hundredan, ofer þrittig peninga.
Gyf se að ðonne forðcume, ceose se man ðonne, ðe ðær betyhtlad sy, swa hweðer swa he wylle swa anfeald ordal swa pundes wurðne að innan ðam ðrim hundredan, ofer ðrittig penega.
Si iusiurandum procedat, eligat accusatus quod horum uel simplex ordalium uel iusiurandum unius libre in tribus hundretis, super XXX den.
Gyf se að ðonne forðcume, ceose se man ðonne, ðe ðær betyhtlad sy, swa hweðer swa he wylle, swa anfeald ordal swa pundes wurðne að, innan ðam ðrim hundredan, ofer ðrittig penega.

Wenn nun dieser Eid zu Stande kommt, dann wähle jener Mann, welcher da beschuldigt ist, eines von beiden [Reinigungsmitteln], wie er will: entweder einfaches Ordal oder einen Eid von 1 Pfund [Silbers] Werth, [mit Helfern] nicht weiter her als aus den drei [dieser und zwei Nachbar-]Hundertschaften: [bei einem Objekt] über 30 Pfennig.

If this oath then succeeds, let the man who is accused choose whichever of the two [means of clearing himself] he wishes: either the single ordeal or an oath worth 1 pound [of silver], [with helpers] from no further away than the three hundreds [this one and two neighbouring ones]: [for an object] over 30 pence.

If the oath is forthcoming, the man who is accused there shall choose whichever he will, either the simple ordeal or an oath equivalent to a pound in value, [supported by compurgators found] within the three hundreds, [in the case of any object] over 30 pence [in value].
div.note: H's ‘swa hweðer he wylle’ (B ‘swa hweðer swa’).

note.seg: uoluerit supplied by edd. from Br
Price zitiert auch Dänisches Recht für die Wahl des Beklagten zwischen Ordal und Eideshilfe; letztere steht ihm nicht frei nach III Atr 4
Price also cites Danish law for the accused’s choice between ordeal and compurgation; according to III Atr 4 the latter is not open to him
S. o. 1, 2⁴. Da voriger Satz von der Wahl der Eideshelfer durch Beklagten sprach, würde Atr sie hier ausschliessen, wenn er (wie Price will) den Auswahleid (s. d. Gl) meinte

See above 1, 2⁴. Since the preceding sentence spoke of the choice of oath-helpers by the accused, Atr would be excluding it here if he meant (as Price would have it) the selection-oath (see that word in Gl)
So II Cn 30, 2, obwohl er 22 strenger den Helferkreis auf Ein Hundred beschränkt
So II Cn 30, 2, although at 22 he more strictly limits the circle of helpers to a single hundred

Zusammenfassen gerade dreier Bezirke s. Gl Dorf 7e. f. Nicht etwa Ein dauernd organisierter Bezirk von 3 Hundreds (s. d. Gl 15ff.), wie solcher später bestand, ist hier gemeint (wie Robertson Histor. essays 120 und Lewis Anc. laws of Wales annahmen), sondern die bloss zufällige Nachbarschaft; s. d. Gl 2

On the grouping of precisely three districts see Gl Dorf 7e. f. What is meant here is not, say, a single permanently organized district of 3 hundreds (see that word in Gl 15ff.), such as existed later (as Robertson Histor. essays 120 and Lewis Anc. laws of Wales supposed), but merely chance neighbourhood; see that word in Gl 2
Vgl. Gl Eidesschwere 4; Beweis 8a. n. Dieser regelt sich nach Mindestwert des Eingeklagten auch I Ew 1, 4. II As 9, 1
Cf. Gl Eidesschwere 4; Beweis 8a. n. In I Ew 1, 4. II As 9, 1 too, proof is governed by the minimum value of the thing claimed

Hundreds are frequently grouped together in this way, cf. Birch, 1130, where grants of land made to the Abbey of Peterborough (972–992) are stated to have been confirmed at meetings of 2, 3 and 8 hundreds. Liebermann quotes also the case of the Abbey of Ely to which were granted jurisdictional rights (socna) over groups of several hundreds (see Birch, 1266, 1267). Instances of hundred-groups are common also in the Liber Eliensis, see pp. 123, 130, 133 etc.
Similar regulation of the oath according to the minimum value of the object involved is found in A. and G. 3; I Edw 1, 4; II As. 9.
